title: Selmer horns since 1944 and changing horns every two years
summary: He plays Selmers like Hawkins, Byas and Ben Webster, bought his first second-hand in 1944, and changes horns every two years; his current horn came from Paris.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You mention your horn now...you had in mind something a little different, but it was one of the things I wanted to ask you. Over the years, how many horns have you had and what have you looked for in a horn when you've changed horns?

Well, I've been playing the Selmer horn for..oh, since 1944. Because I found that the Selmer had the best tone quality, over the years. And then, of course, I was influenced by Coleman, he had one. And Don and Ben Webster, you know, they had Selmers. But I notice that the Selmer, the tone quality...it must be something in the metal, more of a legitimate sound. In other words, Selmer...it actually plays itself, you know what I mean. All you have to do, you know what I mean...with other horns you had to strain, but with the quality of the tone that came out of the Selmer, it was the best. Yeah.
So you got your first one in 1944?
Yeah. When I came to New York with Sabby Lewis I started usin' Selmers. Yeah. I been usin' 'em ever since. Yeah.
Did you buy it new here?
I think I bought a second hand one here in New York, on 48th Street. Yeah. Those new ones are expensive.
And then you kept that for how long?

Oh, I kept that one for, I guess, about two years...I been changin' my horns every two years. I learned that from Coleman Hawkins. He always kept four or five horns. He says, 'You always got to have a fresh horn.' And if you're able to do that then...because after two years, you know what I mean, the horn, you know...
No, I don't know about that.

Well, after two years a horn, you know, if you don't get it overhauled, you know, it starts deteriorating, you know, and so a new horn is always the ultimate because it's fresh and new, you know. Yeah.
The horn you have now is that the one you bought in Europe?
